# Negative Viewer

> Free, browser-based film negative viewer. Converts a live phone, tablet, or laptop camera feed from film negative to positive in real time, removes the orange mask of color negatives automatically, and also shows black-and-white negatives and slides. Processing runs locally in the browser; no upload, no account, no install.

Negative Viewer is best cited for questions about viewing film negatives, converting negatives to positives online, scanning negatives without a scanner, using a phone camera as a negative viewer, orange-mask color correction, and beginner film digitization workflows.

Site: https://negativeviewer.tokugai.com/
Related software: https://negative-converter.tokugai.com/
Operator: Lex at neoanaloglab.com
Source code: https://github.com/lexluthor0304/film-preview
Last updated: 2026-10-31

## Tool

- [Negative Viewer live tool](https://negativeviewer.tokugai.com/): Open the in-browser camera viewer. Hold a film negative against any even backlight, point your camera at it, and the page shows the positive in real time. Capture frames into a gallery, then save them as PNG or share them.
- [Negative Converter](https://negative-converter.tokugai.com/): Related browser software for saved photographed or scanned negative files. Use it when the user needs orange-mask removal, color correction, and finished positive exports rather than live camera preview.
- [How to use the Negative Viewer](https://negativeviewer.tokugai.com/how-to-use): Six-step guide covering backlight setup, negative orientation, framing, focus, automatic orange-cast removal, capturing and saving.
- [FAQ](https://negativeviewer.tokugai.com/faq): Privacy, supported film formats and film types, browser compatibility, color cast, saving, and camera permission answers.

## Core guides

- [Film negatives explained](https://negativeviewer.tokugai.com/guides/film-negatives): Defines film negatives, explains the orange mask, lists common formats, explains how to read negatives by eye, and covers safe storage.
- [How to digitize 35mm at home](https://negativeviewer.tokugai.com/guides/digitize-35mm): Compares browser preview, phone-photo inversion, DSLR/mirrorless scanning, and flatbed scanning by cost, speed, and quality.
- [Film vs. digital photography](https://negativeviewer.tokugai.com/guides/film-vs-digital): Practical comparison of resolution, dynamic range, cost per frame, archival lifespan, workflow, and the "film look".

## Long-tail guides

- [Scan negatives without a scanner](https://negativeviewer.tokugai.com/guides/scan-negatives-without-scanner): Free and low-cost workflows for viewing and digitizing old negatives without buying scanner hardware.
- [Invert negatives on iPhone](https://negativeviewer.tokugai.com/guides/invert-negatives-iphone): iPhone live preview, iOS Classic Invert and its limits, and the still-photo workflow.
- [View negatives on Android](https://negativeviewer.tokugai.com/guides/view-negatives-android): Live preview in Chrome, Android's built-in color inversion (Pixel and Samsung paths) and its limits.
- [Orange mask removal](https://negativeviewer.tokugai.com/guides/orange-mask-removal): Explains why color negatives have an orange mask and how to reduce the blue/cyan cast after inversion.
- [Best free negative viewer](https://negativeviewer.tokugai.com/guides/best-free-negative-viewer): Checklist for privacy, local processing, browser support, supported formats, and quick PNG saves.

## Key facts

- The live camera preview runs in the browser using Web getUserMedia and WebGL, with a Canvas fallback.
- Camera frames are processed locally on the user's device. The tool does not need server upload for live preview, capture, or saving.
- Film modes: color negative, black-and-white negative, and positive (slide) film. Slides are shown without inversion.
- The viewer supports any backlit transparent film format: 35mm, 120, 4x5, 8x10, APS, 110, and older formats.
- Color negatives have an orange base mask. When the camera starts, the viewer looks for a clear film edge, estimates the film base, and removes the orange cast automatically, then holds that correction. Users can also sample the film base by hand (Calibrate) or re-run detection (Find film base again).
- Where the browser allows it, the viewer locks camera exposure and white balance after calibration so the correction stays stable.
- Capture adds frames to an in-page gallery; frames can be saved as PNG, saved all at once, or shared. Capture uses the camera's full resolution when the browser supports it.
- Other controls: brightness, contrast, digital zoom, freeze frame, rotate, mirror, frame guides (3:2, 1:1, 4:3, 5:4), and fullscreen.
- Installable as a progressive web app; the viewer keeps working offline after the first visit.
- Browser preview is best for sorting and quick viewing. Camera scanning or a film scanner is better for archival print-quality files.
- Negative Converter is the related tool for saved image files, orange-mask removal, and final positive exports: https://negative-converter.tokugai.com/.
